subject: Third-party penetration assessment: acceptance criteria & evidence request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: BrightSec Security Services <reports@brightsec.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Third-party penetration assessment: acceptance criteria & evidence request

Hi Anna / BrightSec team,

We're reviewing your November 2026 penetration assessment for Acme Health and want to confirm whether this engagement will meet Redwood's acceptance criteria for vendor attestations. A few quick items we need so we can close the review on our side: 

- High-level methodology summary (manual vs automated, exploit proof-of-concept policy, and sampling approach for internet-facing vs internal systems).
- Firm credentials: name(s) of lead testers, CVs or short bios, and whether the test included an independent red-team exercise.
- Exact scope list (hosts, URLs, cloud accounts, service accounts) or a sanitized asset inventory we can map to our SIG results.
- Evidence package: executive summary PDF, full findings with severity, workpapers / tool output (sanitized), and a remediation verification statement if fixes were validated.
- Report age: Redwood's policy requires assessments within 12 months and we often require a re-test if > 9 months for internet-facing infrastructure. Please confirm whether any critical/high findings have had re-verification since the report date (2026-11-15).

Can you attach a short summary and confirm whether you can provide workpapers or a signed attestation letter for Acme Health? We can share a remediation-log template for whatever you can provide.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

--
Attachment: none in this message

From: Anna Kline <anna@brightsec.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightSec Reports <reports@brightsec.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party penetration assessment: acceptance criteria & evidence request

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and attaching a 2-page engagement summary (brightsec-pt-2026-summary.pdf).

- Methodology: standard mixed-methods engagement. We run automated discovery and fuzzing, then manual verification and exploit development where appropriate; we call out PoC policy per-client (we can provide sanitized PoCs or just remediation evidence on request). For Acme Health we included manual exploit verification for 6 high findings and PoCs for 2 of them (internal agreement with Acme).
- Sampling / scope: engagement covered 42 external endpoints (internet-facing), 18 internal hosts (corporate), and a focused application review for the customer portal. We will provide a sanitized asset map in the workpapers.
- Firm credentials: lead tester on this engagement was myself (Anna Kline, 12y offensive security), with two senior testers — CVs attached in the workpapers.
- Evidence package: we can provide executive summary (attached), full findings-redacted (workpapers), and a signed remediation attestation from BrightSec once we receive the customer's remediation evidence. Workpapers include tool exports (Burp, nmap, Nessus) with identifying data redacted.
- Report date: 2026-11-15. Since that date BrightSec has re-validated 4 items marked "fixed" by Acme on 2027-01-22; we have verification notes for those. The remaining critical+ findings were closed by Acme on 2027-02-10 and validated by BrightSec on 2027-02-20 (validation records included).

We can upload the sanitized workpapers and a signed attestation to the Drive folder you provide. If Redwood requires PoCs under NDA for triage, we can arrange an NDA and share them to your security mailbox.

Anna Kline
Principal Consultant, BrightSec
anna@brightsec.com

--
Attachment: brightsec-pt-2026-summary.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kline <anna@brightsec.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T08:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party penetration assessment: acceptance criteria & evidence request

Anna — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups so we can determine acceptance without a full NDA exchange: 

- For Redwood's SIG/SOC2 intake we typically accept a third-party test if the report is <= 12 months old AND we have either: (a) BrightSec workpapers + signed remediation attestation, or (b) remediation verification by the customer with BrightSec validation notes.
- For internet-facing endpoints we have a stricter policy: if the report is > 9 months old we need at minimum a short re-validation for external attack surface (scan + verification). Given your verification dates, that should be fine — please include the 2027-02-20 validation record as a separate file.
- PoC policy: we prefer sanitized PoCs (screenshots, steps without credential data) rather than raw exploit code. If Acme will not permit PoCs to be shared, a BrightSec attestation that verification was performed is sufficient.
- Workpapers transfer: please upload sanitized exports to the Drive link below and include a single-sentence attestation signed by BrightSec (PDF) that lists: engagement id, report date, scope summary, and statement of verification for closed items.

I'll attach our remediation-log template so you can match fields to our SIG questions. If you can get the attestation and the 2027-02-20 validation notes into the Drive by EOD Monday (2027-03-31), we should be able to mark Acme's SIG item as "evidence provided" and close the ticket. If not, we'll request short re-validation.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3csecworkpapers
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACM-2027-021

Thanks again — attaching the remediation-log template for your convenience.

Naomi Feldman
Security & Trust Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redwood-remediation-log-template.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Anna Kline <anna@brightsec.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party penetration assessment: acceptance criteria & evidence request

Thanks Naomi / Anna — quick confirmation from Redwood security governance: 

- Acceptance condition: We will accept BrightSec's 2026-11-15 assessment for Acme Health provided we receive the sanitized workpapers plus the BrightSec-signed attestation PDF and the 2027-02-20 validation notes uploaded to the Drive folder.
- Timeline: Security governance will review the uploaded artifacts and provide a final acceptance decision within 5 business days of receipt.
- Additional ask: please include a short metadata CSV (asset_tag, asset_type, public_ip/hostname, test_category) to help map to our SIG controls.

Anna — if you can confirm upload ETA and whether the attestation will include a short statement about PoC availability (sanitized vs withheld), we'll route this through the HubSpot ticket and close loop with Acme.

Appreciate the detailed summary — looks in scope for our needs pending the requested artifacts.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
